title: Referring to target in custom battle messages

posts.author: Rethy
posts.body: How would one include the target’s name (or the caster’s name for that matter) in a custom battle message? Like “A casts %1 on B”. I tried a couple different javascript calls, but couldn’t figure out how to insert them properly in the markup. I’m pretty sure I could do a work around with action sequences, but I’m hoping there’s a shorthand.

posts.author: Rethy
posts.body:
A couple more questions regarding battle log messages:
1. I'd previously been trying to use
\.
to delay messages that flash by too quickly, especially information about states that don't have an animation or sound effect attached to them. While it seems to cause a slight delay (I'm guessing just due to the interpreter having to read slightly more), after a bit of testing it definitely does not pause for the full 0.25 or 1 second it would in a regular message box, or at very least adding multiples does not lengthen the delay.
Messages from script calls also disappear almost instantly. I have solved this in common events using
this.wait()
, but it seems to not work in notetags. It might need a specific interpreter identified?
I'm not looking for a plugin that slows down every battle message, I just need to give a bit more time to the few that the engine clears too quickly.
2. The other issue that I haven't been able to find a solution for online is either changing or hiding the Action Failure message in specific situations. There's plenty of times I want the default message to display, like with status effect inducing skills, but I haven't found a way to disable them just for skills that run common events, since selecting the target as "none" prevents common events from running. There are also times when I want the failure message to match the skill better, like "X dodged out of the way", but haven't found a way to do that without just changing it at the system level.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
Isn't the interpreter for reading event lists? Battle Log window has it's own mechanics. You can manipulate the
._waitCount
but usually that stuff is done via pushing the wait method in there that manipulates that, with the
this.push('wait');
Also using scope none doesn't stop common events from running?

I thought that was the case, and when I checked other common event skills they were working as intended with scope none, so I think I have run into a weird interaction between it and
counter actions
. It seems like if a counter attack has a scope of none it will be nullified? Changing the scope to "The User" has it working as intended, with the exception of the "There was no effect on The User!" message.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
I think you can access it with either
BattleManager._logWindow
or
SceneManager._scene._logWindow
So for example
BattleManager._logWindow.push('wait');
